summary: editable-contracts preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers (`_0x488df8` for fs, `_0x52943e` for https) and per-call property-lookup objects wrapping literals like `--version`, `ldd`, and `unzip`. When no local `bun` binary is found, it downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a tarball-shipped file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB single-line bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with heavy string-array/code-point obfuscation (numeric arrays, `fromCodePoint`, rotating shift routine, opaque identifiers) and is unrelated to the package's advertised React/mobx JSON-contracts functionality. Pulling in a second language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling file at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-based supply-chain scanners; the package has no legitimate need for Bun to provide a React/mobx contracts library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
